item.title: On the design of a tensor library in C++
item.description:
Toolchain used for every capture: clang 22.1.8, GCC 16.2.1, libstdc++ 16, GNU binutils 2.46.1 (ld.bfd, nm), LLVM llvm-nm, Fedora 44, x86-64. Library built with -std=c++20 -DCARBON_USE_BLAS against OpenBLAS, the same way CMakeLists.txt builds it. Paths in compiler output are shortened.

Introduction

C++ templates are blueprints used by the compiler to generate classes when they are instantiated with a specific type. Class templates usually take the form of a single header file because the compiler needs to see the full implementation to generate concrete code at the point of use: the template’s definition is visible and a concrete type is known at compile time.

item.title: How execution policies are used in `carbon`
microgpt-c
item.description: microgpt, by Andrej Karpathy is a 200 line python implementation of GPT-2. It is trained on a set of names, and attempts to train a model to generate new ones. Following this, I wanted to try porting it to C as an exercise in learning the language. This post will lay out my approach to implementing an autodifferentiation engine with nothing but the C standard library. It’s recommended that one reads the original post, along with growingswe’s visual explainer for more background on GPT-2 itself.
